verdicts.notes: Our own painted art, not the donor: the donor (donor_standin.png) is flat brown-grey speckle, while the candidate is painted grass tufts with bare muddy patches. Their luminance correlation is 0.004, so it is a new drawing. Same blade-tuft painting style as the sibling (sibling_unpolluted.png), drawn as the polluted version: the vivid green is desaturated to olive/khaki (mean RGB 80/75/45 against the sibling's 80/97/32), and grey-brown mud shows through. It reads as the same artist and the same ground, sick. Its correlation with the sibling is 0.006, so it is a new layout, not a recolour. Its tufts are drawn a little larger and sparser than the sibling's. Painterly, with no outlines. The 1024x1024 canvas is not down-resolved; the donor was also 1024. Opaque, with no props or scenery. Low contrast (luminance std 7.8, donor 7.0, sibling 20.0) suits polluted ground; B2's grey-mud test is about a body against the ground, and this picture is the ground. CONCERN, no constraint governs it (see proposals): tiled_2x2.png shows a faint dark grid line at every repeat join. The texture's outermost 1 px ring is darker than its interior: row 0 lum 63.1, row 1023 63.2, col 0 62.6, col 1023 60.0, against about 66-69 in the interior. The pixel step across the join (5.2 rows / 6.2 cols) is about 1.4x the interior step (3.7 / 4.2). The grass itself continues across the join without a break. Only the darkened edge ring shows, and it becomes a 2 px line when tiled. Fix: replace the outer 1 px ring with its wrapped neighbours, or offset by half a tile and heal.

proposals: Terrain tiling: a terrain file must tile without a visible seam. When it is repeated edge to edge, no line, darkened ring or brightness step may show at the joins. Evidence: tiled_2x2.png for AB_DenseGrass_Polluted shows a thin dark grid at every join, because terrain.png's outermost 1 px rows and columns are about 4-7 luminance darker than its interior. No line of the brief (A1-F1) covers seams, so this could not be a REDO.

Terrain play-zoom input: give terrain subjects a rendered patch of map at 32 px/cell, at the shader's real repeat span, so that D1/B2 and seam visibility can be judged at play zoom instead of being marked not-applicable (subject.json: the repeat span is not measured).

verdicts.notes: This is the repair check. I looked only at what the repair changed. Edge ring: fixed. The outer rows measure lum 73.8 (row 0) and 73.7 (row 1023); the outer columns measure 73.0 (col 0) and 72.3 (col 1023). The next ring in (rows 1/1022, cols 1/1022) measures 72.0-73.8, so the dark 1-px frame that before_repair.png had is gone. Wrap: the pixel step across the join is 3.77 for rows and 5.14 for columns. The interior step is 3.90 and 4.46, so the joins measure 0.97x and 1.15x the interior. That is inside the 1.0-1.2x the donor measures. By eye, tiled_2x2.png shows no grid line and no break at the joins. A 400 px crop centred on the four-way join shows blades running through it with no line or step. Blend band: high-frequency energy in the 96 px border band is 4.21, against 4.49 in the interior (about 6% softer). Band contrast std is 8.0, against 8.6 in the interior. By eye, I see no doubled blades or ghost tufts at the join, only slightly softer grass, so the blend did not ghost. Everything else is as on the first look. It is still our own painted grass, not the donor (donor_standin.png is flat brown-grey speckle). It still reads as the same ground as sibling_unpolluted.png, sick: mean RGB 80/75/44, olive/khaki with grey-brown mud. It is 1024 px RGB, opaque, painterly, and has no outlines or props. One thing remains, and no lettered line covers it: tiled_2x2.png shows the 1024 px repeat as a regular pattern, because the same mud patches recur in each tile. That is a repeat, not a seam. No seam remains.

proposals: Proposal: add a tileability line for terrain under D, for example: 'A terrain file wraps seamlessly. No edge ring darker or lighter than its interior, and the step across the wrap within about 1.2x the interior pixel step (donors measure 1.0-1.2x).' Evidence: before_repair.png had a 1-px dark frame that showed as a grid line in the game, and no lettered line could refuse it. terrain.png now measures 0.97x/1.15x and passes the proposed line.

Proposal (advisory, softer): a heal band blended toward a half-shifted copy should keep its detail. A band's high-frequency energy at no less than about 85% of the interior catches ghosting or a blurred frame. terrain.png measures about 94% (4.21 against 4.49) and would pass.
